title: How do you deal with clothing clipping through legs during animation?
author: Miaou-Miaou1
selftext:
Hey, I'm working on my first game and I'm stuck on something.

My character wears a long dress, and when she runs, her legs poke right through the fabric. Looks awful in motion and I don't really know the right way to fix it.

I'm using Godot for the engine, Blender for modeling and animation, and I generated some of my models with Meshy AI. 

So what's the actual fix here? Do I need to add bones to the dress and weight-paint it so it follows the legs? Or is this something you'd handle with cloth physics? Or do people just make the dress wider and design the animations so the clipping doesn't show? Maybe GPT astra can fix it ?

I'm a solo dev trying to keep things realistic, so I'd rather not overcomplicate it. Any advice (especially anything Godot-specific for the import) would help a lot.

Thanks you

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Its going to be in your paint weights and animations. Just google issue there is a problem like this for alot of poeple thst isn't AI related. Long dresses is always a hard thing to do.. There are alot of resourcses. You might just have a little more work cause meshy AI might have alot more polys.

comments.author: CatoomStudio
comments.body:
You want to make a bone for the piece of dress, then either use physics in the game engine (you need to specify the force, weight, drag, collision with the legs, etc) or you can animate it manually in Blender.

You CAN paintweight it to the legs, but then it wont look like a dress anymore.

Personally I would animate it manually (use references) if there aren’t that many animations tho.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: This can be a r/blenderhelp question as long as you don’t make it obvious it is ai generated
